expr.f: は marks what the sentence is about, the topic.
が marks the subject, especially new or emphasised information, and the thing that exists or is liked.
を marks the thing an action is done to.
に marks a destination, a person receiving, a time, or where something exists.
で marks where an action happens or the means used.
へ marks the direction of movement and is pronounced e.
と marks a companion or joins nouns.
も replaces は, が or を to mean also.
の links nouns: A の B means B of A.
The polite verb ending for the present or future.
The polite past ending.
The polite negative ending.
The polite past negative ending.
Closes a sentence politely after a noun or adjective.
The past of です.
The polite negative of です.
か turns a sentence into a question.
Verb stem + たい means want to do something.
て-form + ください is a polite request.
て-form + います shows an action in progress or a continuing state.
ので gives a reason and sounds softer than から.
ex: Because it is raining, I will not go.

expr.f: After a clause から gives a reason; after a noun it means from.
ex: It is raining, so I will not go.

expr.f: のに shows an unexpected contrast.
ex: Even though it is raining, I will go.

expr.f: けど joins a contrast and is casual.
ex: It is expensive but I will buy it.

expr.f: Verb negative stem + なければならない means must.
ex: 勉強しなければなりません。

expr.f: て-form + しまう shows completion or regret.
Verb + ほうがいい gives advice.
ex: 休んだほうがいいです。

expr.f: て-form + もらう means you receive the favour of an action.
ように shows the aim or state you hope to reach.
ex: 話せるように練習します。
I practise so that I can speak.

expr.f: Stem + そう means it looks as if it will happen.
